However if weights are large, the pre-activation (x@W1+b1) will be large magnitude, causing tanh to saturate near +/-1. So hidden unit activation will be roughly sign of (weight * input + bias). Input x for that channel is either 0 or 1 (since binary). If agent present at that cell, x=1 else 0. So if agent present at that location, the contribution to hidden unit pre-activation is weight_j (from that input) plus bias b1_j. If agent absent, contribution is 0 plus bias.

Thus the difference in hidden activation due to agent presence is roughly weight_j (since bias constant). If weight_j is large positive, hidden unit will be more active (tending to +1) when agent present; if large negative, hidden unit will be more inactive (tending to -1) when agent present.

Thus we can approximate effect on logits: change in logit for action a due to agent at that location ≈ sum_j weight_j * W3[j,a] (since hidden activation change approx weight_j, ignoring tanh saturation but sign matters).
